why: Modes (determinism, output, ordering, response) are declared in three separate contracts and nothing checks whether a mode is legal in the phase or capability it is used with. The tempting fix — a MODE node class — would break the closed 14-class XCFE node ISA and double-encode authority, which the ISA header already refuses for `Policy` ('making it a node class would double-encode it'). Modes therefore become a P13 *program-descriptor* class plus a guard that XCFE applies to narrow admission.

descriptor_class.name: MODE
descriptor_class.grammar_invariant: P13 — program-descriptor classes only, disjoint from xcfe_node_class.h
why_not_a_node_class: the node ISA assigns every class a fixed authority phase, and a mode is not Wo/Yax/Sek/Ch'en/Xul work
the ISA header already refuses a `Policy` class for the same reason: operation authority is XCFE's own mechanism, so a node class would double-encode it
the mode vocabulary already exists in operator-algebra.contracts.json (determinism), filter.ebnf (output) and reduce.ebnf (ordering); a node class would create a second vocabulary for one word
descriptor_class.authority_law: descriptor governs the lane form; XCFE governs execution

mode_phase_laws.law: a mode may only narrow what XCFE would otherwise admit; no mode can grant admission, verification or commit
mode_phase_laws.M1: no mode grants commit authority: commit_authorized stays false for every mode, and the guard has no granting outcome
mode_phase_laws.M2: Ch'en verification requires reproducible evidence: the stochastic determinism mode is refused there (unreproducible_evidence), and an observational mode is refused unless it declares that external observations are recorded
mode_phase_laws.M3: Xul is not a filter: the drop output mode is refused in Xul (commit_is_not_a_filter)
mode_phase_laws.M4: ordering follows the consumer: where a consumer requires structural order, the confidence ordering mode is refused (ordering_must_be_structural)
mode_phase_laws.M5: a neutral or reset response mode carries no evidence and cannot stand as one (neutral_mode_carries_no_evidence)
mode_phase_laws.M6: an undeclared mode or family is refused by name (unknown_mode), never mapped onto a legal one
mode_phase_laws.M7: a mode is a selector: it applies to a phase and an optional capability, and it is refused everywhere the law table does not admit it

guard.detail_example: the denied status is always a named reason, so a refusal is diagnosable

status_vocabulary_note: the outcome set is exactly these seven; there is deliberately no granting status, which is what MODE3/MODE5 state

trace.law: the trace records the mode that filtered candidate selection and marks it narrows_only; no mode is recorded as granting admission or commit (M1, MODE4, MODE5)

fields.steps: mode-filtering decisions appear in the ordered step log

invariants.MODE1: MODE is a program-descriptor class: it does not appear in the 14-class node ISA and claims no canonical phase
invariants.MODE2: the four families and their values are exactly the union of what the three existing contracts declare plus this contract's response family
invariants.MODE3: the guard's outcome set is {allowed, denied}; there is no granting outcome and every refusal names a typed reason
invariants.MODE4: a mode may narrow an admission the host already granted and may never widen one it denied
invariants.MODE5: no mode, in any family, sets commit_authorized true
